title: Today I learned.
lead: Short notes from building and running backends and infrastructure: the gotcha, the fix and a snippet to reuse.

pgbouncer.title: PgBouncer transaction pooling breaks django-tenants
pgbouncer.body: django-tenants picks the tenant with a session-level `SET search_path` on the database connection. In transaction mode, PgBouncer can run that SET and the next query on different server connections, so the query may reach another tenant's schema or `public`. Use session pooling for the tenant app, or skip PgBouncer there and rely on Django's persistent connections (`CONN_MAX_AGE`).

argocd.title: Argo CD automated sync neither prunes nor self-heals by default
argocd.body: With automated sync alone, Argo CD applies new commits but leaves resources deleted from Git running, and ignores changes made by hand with `kubectl`. `prune: true` removes what Git no longer declares, and `selfHeal: true` brings any drift in the cluster back to the state in Git.

vxlan.title: VXLAN takes 50 bytes off every packet's MTU
vxlan.body: VXLAN wraps each frame in outer IPv4, UDP and VXLAN headers and carries the inner Ethernet header too: 50 bytes in total, 70 over an IPv6 underlay. On a 1500-byte underlay, set the overlay MTU to 1450 or enable jumbo frames, otherwise small pings work while large transfers stall.

terraform.title: Terraform can lock S3 state without DynamoDB
terraform.body: Since Terraform 1.10, the S3 backend can lock state with a `.tflock` object stored next to the state file (`use_lockfile = true`), built on S3 conditional writes; it is generally available since 1.11, which also deprecated DynamoDB-based locking. No DynamoDB table is needed. Turn on bucket versioning so a bad state write can be rolled back.

jsonlogs.title: Loki wants JSON log lines and few labels
jsonlogs.body: Loki indexes labels only, so high-cardinality fields such as a request or tenant ID belong in the log line, not in labels. With one JSON object per line, LogQL's `json` parser turns those fields into filters at query time.

tmux.title: tmux keeps remote work alive when SSH drops
tmux.body: Work on a server inside a named tmux session: if the connection drops, the shell and its running commands survive, and `tmux attach` brings them back. A few default key bindings, pressed after the Ctrl-b prefix, cover most daily use.
